property_summary: When owner calls withdrawAll with contract balance = 1 wei, the reference version (using transfer) succeeds and sends the ether, while the buggy version (using send) fails silently and does not send the ether.

Owner calls withdrawAll with a contract balance of 1 ether to a recipient contract that has a fallback function reverting on receive; reference (transfer) succeeds and reduces balance to 0, buggy (send) fails silently and leaves balance unchanged.

When owner calls withdrawAll with a contract balance of 1 ether to a recipient contract that has a fallback function using more than 2300 gas, the reference (transfer) succeeds and reduces balance to 0, while the buggy (send) fails silently and leaves balance unchanged.
Owner calls withdrawAll with contract balance = 1 wei to an EOA recipient — reference (transfer) succeeds and leaves balance 0, buggy (send) fails silently and leaves balance unchanged.
Owner calls withdrawAll when contract balance is 1 wei and recipient is an EOA; reference (transfer) succeeds and balance becomes 0, buggy (send) fails silently and balance stays 1.
When owner sends 1 ether to the contract, then a non-owner calls withdrawAll(bob), the reference contract reverts (only owner can withdraw) while the buggy contract transfers the balance to bob.
When owner calls withdrawAll(0xDead) with contract balance = 1 wei, reference sends 1 wei to 0xDead, bug sends 1 wei to msg.sender (owner), so address(c).balance and owner balance differ after call.
